title: International Fixed Calendar
intro: A proposed calendar with thirteen identical four-week months, created to make dates and weekdays follow a predictable pattern.
summary: Thirteen months of 28 days, totalling 364 regular days, plus a year-end day outside the normal weekly sequence and an extra leap-day when applicable.
origin: Moses B. Cotsworth promoted the International Fixed Calendar in the early 1900s. The proposal was used by some organisations but never became a global civil calendar.
structure: Each month has exactly four seven-day weeks. A thirteenth month named Sol is inserted between June and July.
pattern_note: Leap Day and Year Day sit outside the repeated seven-day week. The main monthly dates therefore keep consistent weekday patterns.
history: The design aimed to simplify business, budgeting and annual planning because every standard month has the same length. Many traditions objected to calendar reforms that interrupted the seven-day weekly cycle.
example: In the proposal, the month Sol follows June and precedes July. Its first day begins another four-week, 28-day block.
limits: This is the Cotsworth calendar proposal, not the civil system used by all countries. The extra days and special weekday treatment are features of the proposal rather than Gregorian dates.
